title: Structural Traps — The Public-Goods Dilemma
metadata_mapping: Existing concept and responsive asset conventions; no new schema, navigation, or publication action.

patterns.title: The Public-Goods Dilemma
patterns.domain: Strategic and game-theoretic problems; collective provision, dispersed benefits, and funding institutions

sources.title: Paul A. Samuelson (1954), The Pure Theory of Public Expenditure
sources.supports: Collective consumption without subtraction from others’ consumption; explicit acknowledgement of earlier public-finance writers.
sources.boundary: Original scan opened; first substantive page, printed p. 387, was rendered and read by local OCR because web extraction returned only the archive cover. No unread detailed welfare theorem is imported into the example.

sources.title: Ernst Fehr, Cooperation and Public Goods Provision, author teaching slides hosted at MIT
sources.supports: Linear voluntary-contribution game, simultaneous choices, alpha < 1 private incentive and n*alpha > 1 group-return condition.
sources.boundary: Formal framework for the qualitative comparison of private contribution cost and dispersed benefit, not data about the radio station. Empirical observations are separately attributed to the original experiment.

sources.title: Urs Fischbacher, Simon Gächter, Ernst Fehr (2001), Are People Conditionally Cooperative? Evidence from a Public Goods Experiment
sources.supports: Final eight-page paper read, including one-shot strategy-method design, 44 undergraduate participants, 22 conditional-cooperation schedules, and 13 all-zero schedules.
sources.boundary: Monetary student laboratory sample and elicited contribution schedules. No population-wide personality prevalence, measured reporting benefit, repeated-game outcome, or causal effect of the proposed budget rule is inferred.

sources.title: Elinor Ostrom (2009), Beyond Markets and States: Polycentric Governance of Complex Economic Systems, Nobel lecture
sources.supports: Read the university-hosted facsimile: public goods versus common-pool resources, excludability and subtractability as varying dimensions, and diverse institutional arrangements for provision.
sources.boundary: No claim that common-pool harvesting studies directly prove a funding intervention for public goods. No universal design principle, governance winner, or empirical effect size is transferred. Nobel-hosted PDF access failed; the readable academic mirror is linked.

patterns.short_description: Recognize when shared benefits exceed their private return to contributors, then distinguish voluntary cooperation from funding arrangements that change who must contribute and how.
use_when: Which funding obligation changes while listening stays open?
goals: Recognize the concrete predicament before terminology.
Preserve defining assumptions and distinctions without calculations.
Evaluate intervention authority, costs, residual risks, and changed assumptions.
mechanisms: Secure accepted, collectible funding for a defined period while retaining open listening.
Joining is voluntary; collection, fairness, editorial accountability, and later renewal still matter.

example_structure.scenario: Incremental reporting within an operating listener-supported broadcast, not an all-or-nothing station launch. Own incremental benefit below private cost; combined benefit above cost. One-shot, known structure, own net interests; actual generosity not ruled out. Optional membership adoption is separate from accepted collectible dues; nonmember free riding remains.
example_structure.changed_relationship: Secure accepted, collectible funding for a defined period while retaining open listening.
example_structure.residual_constraints: Joining is voluntary; collection, fairness, editorial accountability, and later renewal still matter.
example_structure.evidence: Hypothetical scenario and stipulated continuation; no expected result presented as measured outcome. Qualitative ranking and ordering replace illustrative arithmetic.

visual.question: Which funding obligation changes while listening stays open?
visual.alternative_text: Hypothetical qualitative illustration. Original voluntary donations and accepted member dues are alternative routes funding incremental local reporting. All listeners, including nonmembers, can benefit under either route. Dues work only after willing adoption and reliable collection for the agreed period. Change: Secure accepted, collectible funding for a defined period while retaining open listening. Limitation: Joining is voluntary; collection, fairness, editorial accountability, and later renewal still matter.
visual.caption: Hypothetical illustration. Dashed and green inputs compare funding arrangements for the same open broadcast. Accepted dues can support an agreed period without excluding nonmembers, but voluntary adoption and continued funding remain unresolved tasks. No single production threshold is assumed.

patterns.evidence_boundary: Foundational definitions and formal results retain their assumptions. Empirical studies retain setting and design limitations. Examples and suggested practical responses are original editorial synthesis. Expected familiarity is an editorial judgment, not a comprehension-study finding.
